subject: Financial risk allocation: order form redlines and suggested compromise
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@beaconhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@beaconhealth.com>, Matt Howard <m.matt@bensonllp.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed edits to Order Form - limitation of financial responsibility

Karthik — thanks again for the demo last week. We've reviewed your latest MSA + Order Form and our procurement/legal team pushed back on the limitation of financial responsibility section. High level: they want either (A) a single aggregate cap tied to fees paid over the full term, or (B) a rolling annual cap based on fees paid in the prior 12 months, and they also want express carve-outs for wilful misconduct, data breaches, and third-party IP indemnity.

Attached are our in-line redlines (Redlines_MSA_v3.docx) and a short spreadsheet that shows how the two cap approaches would look with our projected spend. Can your legal ops team confirm Redwood's preferred approach and whether you can accept a limited carveout for consequential damages only where directly resulting from data loss?

Proposed quick path: if Redwood will accept an annualized-fees cap (12-month lookback) at 3x prior-year fees for a single-year breach, Beacon will sign the MSA + order form and we can move to procurement signatures this month. If not, we'll need to escalate to our CPO.

Thanks — Nora
Nora Patel
Director, Procurement
Beacon Health
--

Looping legal/product/finance — see Beacon's ask. Their procurement prefers an annualized cap at 3x prior-year fees and carveouts for willful misconduct, data breach, and IP indemnity. They ask specifically about consequential damages carveouts tied to data loss.

Can we get position guidance: (1) annualized vs aggregate over term (we have precedent for both), (2) multiplier (we usually do 1-2x for small customers, but there are examples at 3x), and (3) whether we can add a narrowly drafted consequential-damages carveout for direct data-loss remediation only?

Quick notes: product favours annualized approach for predictable exposures; finance wants to keep aggregate over term; legal favors limiting carveouts tightly. I can push a small commercial compromise if legal signs off.

Karthik
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed edits to Order Form - limitation of financial responsibility

Thanks — read their redlines. My tentative guidance below (legal ops):

1) Basis of cap: we can accept an annualized-fees cap (12-month lookback) as a commercial concession for accounts that are on predictable, recurring billing, but we need to anchor the language so the cap cannot be doubled by contract extensions or renewals. Suggested language: "Total aggregate liability for each 12-month period shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD [X], or (ii) three times the Fees actually paid to Redwood during the prior 12 months. For the avoidance of doubt, any liability shall be calculated on a per-12-month rolling basis and shall not accumulate across separate 12-month periods except where explicitly stated."

2) Multiplier: 3x is acceptable for this deal given their ARR profile, but we should require a security attestation quarterly and a quarterly spend minimum to qualify for 3x (or revert to 1.5x). This gives us a lever.

3) Carve-outs: willful misconduct and IP indemnity are standard carve-outs and we can accept. For consequential damages, we should allow a narrow carveout that permits recovery of reasonable third-party remediation costs directly tied to a verified data exfiltration event — capped and time-limited (12 months). Broad consequential damages language stays excluded.

4) Remedy waterfall: require that customers exhaust contractual remedies (repair, rollback, credits) before claiming indemnity beyond the cap unless the event is willful or fraudulent.

If everyone agrees, I'll draft redline language and ask Markus to run the numbers for worst-case exposure. Markus — can you model the 3x vs 1.5x exposure over a 3-year term with our projected usage? Marissa — if legal signs the language, can you send a short concession memo and updated order form for Nora?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Corporate Counsel, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: suggested_language_snippet.txt

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed edits to Order Form - limitation of financial responsibility

Done — attached is the quick exposure calc for the two scenarios based on Beacon's forecast. Highlights:
- 3x annualized cap -> peak exposure in year 2 of $4.2M (worst case).
- 1.5x annualized cap -> peak exposure in year 2 of $2.1M.
- Aggregate-over-term at 3x total fees -> $6.8M over 3 years.

Recommendation: accept annualized 3x only if we attach the security attestation clause and a quarterly minimum spend of $35k; otherwise offer 1.5x. If Beacon pushes for aggregate-over-term we should push for a per-incident subcap and require an insurance endorsement.

Markus Klein
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: OrderForm_FeeSummary.xlsx (calc tab)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@beaconhealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@beaconhealth.com>, Matt Howard <m.matt@bensonllp.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed edits to Order Form - limitation of financial responsibility

Nora / Elena / Matt — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Summary of Redwood's proposed compromise below: 

1) Basis and multiplier: We can accept an annualized-fees cap (12-month rolling) set at 3x of the fees actually paid in the prior 12 months, provided Beacon commits to the quarterly security attestation below and meets a quarterly minimum spend of USD 35k. Language will include a floor of USD 100k to avoid trivial caps.

2) Carve-outs: We will accept carve-outs for willful misconduct, third-party IP indemnity, and a narrowly drafted consequential-damages exception for third-party remediation costs arising from a verified, Redwood-caused data exfiltration event, capped at USD 500k and timeboxed to costs incurred within 12 months of the event. All other consequential damages remain excluded.

3) Remedy ladder: Customers must exhaust the standard operational remedies (repair, restore from backup, credits) before pursuing amounts beyond the cap except when the conduct is willful or fraudulent.

4) Next steps: Laura will send the redline with the exact wording (expect within 24 hours). Mark will attach the exposure worksheet and commercial fallback language if Beacon rejects the minimum-spend condition. If Beacon agrees, Karina (Contracts Ops) will issue a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

If you're comfortable with this approach, please let me know by end of day tomorrow and we'll push the updated Order Form. Happy to hop on a 20-min call with your counsel if that would help.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: proposed_concession_summary.txt
